import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 143

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/143](https://www.erdosproblems.com/143)
-/

open Filter Finset
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos143

/--
Let $A \subseteq (1, \infty)$ be a countably infinite set such that for all $x\neq y\in A$ and
integers $k \geq 1$ we have $|kx - y| \geq 1$.
-/
def WellSeparatedSet (A : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  (A ⊆ (Set.Ioi (1 : ℝ))) ∧ Set.Infinite A ∧ Set.Countable A ∧
  (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ A, x ≠ y → (∀ k ≥ (1 : ℕ), 1 ≤ |k * x - y|))

/--
Does this imply that
$$
\liminf \frac{|A \cap [1,x]|}{x} = 0?
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_143.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℝ), WellSeparatedSet A →
    liminf (fun x => (A ∩ (Set.Icc 1 x)).ncard / x) atTop = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
Or
$$
\sum_{x \in A} \frac{1}{x \log x} < \infty,
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_143.parts.ii (A : Set ℝ) (h : WellSeparatedSet A) :
    Summable fun (x : A) ↦ 1 / (x * Real.log x) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the two other conjectures.
/-
$$
\sum_{\substack{x < n \\ x \in A}} \frac{1}{x} = o(\log n)?
$$

Perhaps even

$$
\sum_{\substack{x < n \\ x \in A}} \frac{1}{x} \ll \frac{\log x}{\sqrt{\log \log x}}?
$$
-/

end Erdos143

status_issues.source_status: Solved affirmatively as a consequence of the 2025 theorem of Dimitris Koukoulopoulos, Youness Lamzouri, and Jared Duker Lichtman. The website remains globally OPEN because the summability question is still open.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/143 reports that Koukoulopoulos–Lamzouri–Lichtman proved ∑_{a∈A, a<n} 1/a = o(log n). Theorem 1 and §1.2 of https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09539 establish this under the separation hypothesis. It implies part (i): if N(t)=|A∩[1,t]| had positive lower density, then N(t)≥ct eventually for some c>0, and partial summation would give ∑_{a≤X}1/a ≥ c log X−O(1), contradicting that estimate.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change part (i) to `@[category research solved, AMS 11]`, replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`, and cite KLL25 in its documentation. Leave part (ii) tagged open.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses real-valued `Summable` over the subtype `A`, rather than writing the series as an extended-real sum less than infinity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every element of A is greater than 1, so every term 1/(x·log x) is strictly positive. For nonnegative terms, unconditional real summability is equivalent to finiteness of the extended nonnegative sum; there is no conditional-convergence distinction. In /workspace/review/witness.lean, proved the exact equivalence between the displayed `Summable` proposition and `(∑' x : A, ENNReal.ofReal (1 / ((x : ℝ) * Real.log x))) < ⊤`.
